extraction_metadata.notes: Quantum-inspired optimization (QIO) using qutrit ternary encoding (LS/SS/non-invest) with Global best-guided Quantum-inspired Tabu Search (GQTS). Classical simulation only; no gate-based QPU. Results reported as bar charts (Fig 2) comparing risk and trend ratio across 13 sliding windows for hybrid strategy vs pure LS and SS. Numeric values read from figures are approximate.

paper_metadata.title: Qutrit-based Quantum-inspired Optimization Model on Real-world Portfolio Optimization
paper_metadata.venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE)

summary: Qutrit-inspired GQTS metaheuristic for hybrid long-selling / short-selling / non-investment portfolio optimization. Classical simulation with ternary (qutrit) encoding over Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA, 30 stocks) from 2013-2022; initial fund $10M, solution space 330, population 10, 10000 iterations, 50 reps per period, theta=0.0003. Uses sliding-window (13 SW types, 830 periods). Benchmarked against EL-GNQTS-run pure LS and SS portfolios. Hybrid qutrit strategy yields consistently lower risk and higher trend ratio than LS-only or SS-only across all 13 SWs (results shown in figure bars; no tables provided).

experiments.description: Qutrit-GQTS on DJIA (2013-2022) with sliding window evaluation. Ternary encoding (|0>=non-invest, |1>=LS, |2>=SS) with modified beta1/beta2 update rules driven by global-best vs local-worst. Evaluated by trend ratio over 13 sliding-window types.

algorithm.variant: Qutrit-based Global-best Guided Quantum-inspired Tabu Search (qutrit-GQTS)
algorithm.ansatz: Qutrit state |psi>=alpha|0>+beta|1>+gamma|2>, |alpha|^2+|beta|^2+|gamma|^2=1; two probability boundaries beta_j1, beta_j2 partition the three states.
algorithm.optimizer: Global-best guided Quantum-inspired Tabu Search (GQTS) with qutrit update rules (Eq. 2)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Ternary per-asset encoding (qutrit-inspired): 0=non-investment, 1=long-selling, 2=short-selling, stored as beta1/beta2 probability thresholds per asset.
problem_formulation.constraints: Sliding-window training/testing; fund allocation constraints handled implicitly by trend-ratio evaluation.

problem_instance.dataset_name: Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), 30 US stocks

dataset_specification.description: 13 sliding-window types (M*, M2M, Q*, Q2Q, Q2M, H*, H2H, H2M, H2Q, Y2Y, Y2H, Y2Q, Y2M) over 830 periods. Initial fund $10M.

results.value: hybrid > LS and SS across all 13 sliding windows
results.notes: Fig 2(b) shows hybrid qutrit strategy achieves a higher trend ratio than pure LS and SS portfolios in every one of 13 SW types. Approximate hybrid range ~0.3-2.3 (y-axis read from figure).

results.value: hybrid < LS and SS across all 13 sliding windows
results.notes: Fig 2(a) shows hybrid risk (x1e5 USD) consistently below LS and SS across 13 SWs. Approximate hybrid range ~0.3-1.5 (x1e5); LS/SS range ~0.5-3.8 (x1e5).
